performance_optimizations.title: Object Pool for Particles to Reduce GC Pressure
performance_optimizations.description: The particle system creates new THREE.Mesh, THREE.BoxGeometry, and THREE.MeshPhongMaterial objects for each particle (30 per explosion, 60+ for shrapnel explosions). This causes significant garbage collection pressure during combat-heavy moments.
performance_optimizations.rationale: In particles.js, createExplosion() and createShrapnelExplosion() instantiate 30-90 new mesh objects per explosion. During intense gameplay with multiple explosions, this leads to GC pauses causing frame drops. THREE.js object creation is expensive - geometry buffer allocation, material shader compilation, and scene graph updates all add overhead.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: 30-90 new objects created per explosion, causing ~5-15ms GC pauses
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: Near-zero allocation during gameplay, eliminating GC-related frame drops
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Create a ParticlePool class with pre-allocated particles (pool size ~200)
2. Store inactive particles in a free list
3. On explosion, acquire particles from pool, set position/velocity
4. On particle death, return to pool instead of dispose()
5. Share geometry and use a single material with vertex colors
6. Consider THREE.InstancedMesh for better batching
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Initial memory footprint increases (~5MB), slightly more complex code

performance_optimizations.title: Eliminate Vector3 Allocations in Hot Collision Loops
performance_optimizations.description: Collision detection code creates new THREE.Vector3() objects inside loops that run every frame. In checkBarrierCollision(), getWorldPosition() allocates a new Vector3 for each barrier block (up to ~150 blocks) every frame.
performance_optimizations.rationale: Lines like `const blockWorldPos = new THREE.Vector3()` inside loops cause continuous memory allocation. With 4 barriers × ~40 blocks each, this creates 160+ Vector3 allocations per collision check. Combined with missile collision checks, this can cause frequent minor GC pauses.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: ~200+ temporary Vector3 allocations per frame during active gameplay
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: Zero allocations in collision code, smoother frame times
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Create module-level reusable Vector3 instances:
   const _tempVec3 = new THREE.Vector3();
   const _blockWorldPos = new THREE.Vector3();
2. Replace `new THREE.Vector3()` in loops with reusable instances
3. In barriers.js checkBarrierCollision(): reuse single Vector3 for getWorldPosition
4. In missiles.js updateAlienMissiles(): reuse direction/target vectors
5. In game.js updateCamera(): reuse lookAtPoint Vector3
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Requires careful coding to avoid race conditions if vectors are used across async boundaries

performance_optimizations.title: Batch Date.now() Calls with Single Frame Timestamp
performance_optimizations.description: Date.now() is called repeatedly in animateAlien() (line 521), update loops, and various time-based animations. Each alien calls Date.now() every frame, totaling 30-50 calls per frame.
performance_optimizations.rationale: While Date.now() is fast (~0.001ms), calling it 50+ times per frame adds up. More importantly, animations using inconsistent timestamps can cause subtle visual stuttering. The game loop should compute a single frame timestamp and pass it to all systems.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: 30-50 Date.now() calls per frame, inconsistent animation timing
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: Single timestamp per frame, perfectly synchronized animations, ~0.05-0.1ms saved per frame
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. In main.js animate(), compute frameTime = performance.now()
2. Pass frameTime to update(frameTime) in game.js
3. Pass frameTime to animateAlien(alien, time) - use precomputed time * 0.001
4. Update missile trail timing to use passed frame time
5. Store frame time in a shared constant module for systems that need it
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Minor API changes across multiple modules, need to thread time parameter through call stack

performance_optimizations.title: Use InstancedMesh for Barrier Blocks
performance_optimizations.description: Each barrier is built from ~40 individual BoxGeometry meshes (4 barriers × ~40 blocks = 160 draw calls). THREE.InstancedMesh can render all blocks in a single draw call per barrier.
performance_optimizations.rationale: In barriers.js createBarrier(), each block is a separate Mesh with cloned material. This creates 160+ draw calls just for barriers. WebGL draw call overhead is significant - each call has CPU-GPU synchronization cost. InstancedMesh batches identical geometry into a single draw call.
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: 4 draw calls for barriers (one per barrier group), ~20-30% reduction in overall draw calls
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Create single BoxGeometry for block size
2. Create InstancedMesh with max block count (50 per barrier)
3. Set instance matrices for each block position
4. On block destruction, set instance scale to 0 or swap with last instance
5. Track active instance count for proper rendering
6. Update instanceMatrix.needsUpdate on changes
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: More complex destruction logic, need to track instance-to-block mapping, slight complexity increase

performance_optimizations.title: Optimize Starfield with GPU-based Animation
performance_optimizations.description: The starfield animates 2000 stars by iterating through a 6000-element Float32Array every frame in JavaScript. This work could be moved to the GPU using a custom shader.
performance_optimizations.rationale: In starfield.js updateStarfield(), a JavaScript loop updates 6000 array values and sets needsUpdate=true every frame. This forces a CPU-GPU buffer upload every frame. A vertex shader can animate positions directly on the GPU using a time uniform, eliminating both the JS loop and the buffer upload.
performance_optimizations.currentMetric: 6000 array operations + buffer upload every frame (~0.5-1ms)
performance_optimizations.expectedImprovement: Zero CPU cost for starfield animation, ~0.5-1ms saved per frame
performance_optimizations.implementation:
1. Create custom ShaderMaterial for stars
2. Store original positions + random seed in vertex attributes
3. In vertex shader: calculate animated Z based on time uniform and seed
4. Wrap Z position when it exceeds threshold
5. Pass time uniform each frame (trivial cost)
6. Remove JavaScript animation loop entirely
performance_optimizations.tradeoffs: Requires GLSL knowledge, custom shader maintenance, slightly harder to debug

metadata.potentialSavings: ~5-15ms per frame during combat, smoother 60fps gameplay

profiledAreas.particle_system: High GC pressure from object creation
profiledAreas.draw_calls: Many small meshes instead of instanced rendering
profiledAreas.starfield: CPU-bound animation that could be GPU-bound

metadata.recommendations_summary: Focus on memory allocation patterns first (perf-001, perf-002) as they cause visible stuttering during gameplay. GPU optimizations (perf-004, perf-005) provide steady improvements to baseline performance.
